The '''V-6 haywire grenade''' was a small hand-held [[Electromagnetic pulse grenade/Legends|electromagnetic pulse grenade]] produced by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc.]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. As the bulk of [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|the army]] fielded by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] consisted of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle]] [[Droid/Legends|droids]], it became practical for the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] to employ [[Electromagnetic pulse/Legends|electromagnetic pulse]] weapons specifically designed to overload electronic circuitry, and the V-6 haywire grenade was an early product of this strategy.

==Description==
V-6 haywire grenades were calibrated to cause massive electrical disruptions to the circuitry of droids, unleashing electromagnetic pulse blasts upon detonation.<ref name="BF1 guide" /> The power of these blasts were capable of violently bursting combat droids asunder, and in this way, the grenade was very similar to its cousin, the [[electromagnetic pulse launcher]] designed for the use of [[Clone jet trooper/Legends|clone jet troopers]]. Like [[Ion grenade/Legends|ion grenades]], haywire grenades inflicted less damage against organic beings. Nevertheless, they were still capable of electrocuting and even killing any organisms within the blast radius.<ref name="BF1" />

==History==
At the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], V-6 haywire grenades comprised the standard equipment of regular, front-line [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]]. The grenades therefore saw widespread use on many early fronts such as the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]], the [[First Battle of Kamino]], and the [[Battle of Rhen Var (Clone Wars)|Battle of Rhen Var]] where clones employed them effectively against not only [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] but also [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]] and [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]]. While the haywire grenades were potent, specialized clones such as [[Clone sharpshooter/Legends|clone sharpshooters]] and [[Clone jet trooper/Legends|clone jet troopers]] were issued [[V-1 thermal detonator]]s instead,<ref name="BF1" /> and [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] favored their own powerful EMP grenades that they referred to as Electrostatic Charge Detonators.<ref name="RC">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>

Towards the end of the war, V-6 haywire grenades were less commonly utilized, particularly after the transition from [[Phase I clone trooper armor]] to [[Phase II clone trooper armor/Legends|Phase II]].<ref name="BF2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> The clone army was equipped with other models of EMP grenades including a variant that was less destructive yet still effective at disabling battle droids<ref name="Innocents of Ryloth">{{TCW|Innocents of Ryloth}}</ref><ref name="Landing at Point Rain">{{TCW|Landing at Point Rain}}</ref> and the [[reverse-polarity pulse grenade]] used by [[Alpha-class Advanced Recon Commando]]s.<ref name="Republic 50">[[Republic 50|''Republic'' 50]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The sole appearance of the V-6 haywire grenade is the [[2004]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]'' though its model is only identified in the game's [[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|strategy guide]]. Only the standard clone troopers of the Soldier class are equipped with them while other clone units employ the V-1 thermal detonator.<ref name="BF1" /> In the sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', the haywire grenade was removed to be replaced by the V-1 thermal detonator as the primary grenade of the standard clone trooper of the Soldier class.<ref name="BF2" />
